newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek police fear hundreds of migrants drowned.
newsitem.headline: Greek police fear hundreds of migrants drowned.

text.p: Greek police said on Saturday that some 280 migrants from India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka may have drowned in the Mediterranean Sea when their ship collided with another also packed with immigrants.

A public order ministry statement said a further 107 illegal immigrants had been arrested in Greece and had said they saw hundreds of their compatriots go down with the sunken vessel after a collision on Christmas Day.
Italian port authorities said on Saturday they had been searching the sea between Sicily and the island of Malta for signs of a collision but had found nothing.

"Malta asked us on December 26 to look into a possible collision between a big ship and a smaller one but nothing has been found, though we are still looking," a spokesman for the Italian navy rescue coordination centre said.

The Greek statement said the immigrants from Sri Lanka had told interrogators they paid $8,000 each in Colombo for an air ticket to Cairo and the sea trip to Europe. The Indians and Pakistanis said they had paid $5,000 each.
"The sunken ship's characteristics are similar with those of a ship stolen the previous night from Malta," the statement said.
A cargo ship called Friendship, flying a Panama flag, left Alexandria in Egypt on December 9 for a European country with more than 250 immigrants aboard, it said.
The immigrants were transferred on December 12 to another cargo ship, the Honduran-flagged Yioham, which already had 215 immigrants on board.
The Yioham's captain, a Lebanese resident of Athens, then on Christmas Day trans-shipped 318 of the immigrants to a smaller ship in the Malta-Sicily channel.
"During manoeuvres, the smaller ship (stolen from Malta) was rammed by the Yioham and sank. Only 29 immigrants were picked up by the Yioham," the statement said.
Police said the Yioham on December 29 entered the Greek port of Nafplion where 107 immigrants were arrested while a further 65 escaped arrest.

"We have arrested 107 illegal immigrants who say they were involved in the collision and swear to the Koran that they saw hundreds of their compatriots go down with one of the vessels which sunk," a senior police official told Reuters.
"Those arrested were almost starved to death and terrified," he added.

"The 107 immigrants were taken to a warehouse outside Nafplion and were told to wait for trucks to pick them up. After one day they came out to find some food and they were spotted by villagers who alerted us," the police official said.
The ministry statement said police had alerted Interpol in Italy, Malta and Egypt.
